MFEHFsO-XSI.summary: Technology Connections explains why heat pumps matter right now, covering their efficiency, how they hold up in cold weather and the energy savings over burning fuel. It follows his earlier explainer on how they work.
MFEHFsO-XSI.why: HN's default link for anyone asking whether heat pumps work and why they're efficient, thanks to the presenter's clear and enthusiastic delivery.

Mfsnlbd-4xQ.summary: Chris Ford builds up from a single sine wave through layered abstractions to a Bach canon, using Clojure and the Overtone audio environment. The talk shows music theory as a natural fit for functional programming.
Mfsnlbd-4xQ.why: HN repeatedly recommends it as a delightful talk that makes music theory click and introduces Clojure and Overtone.

Mc_4Z1oiXhY.summary: Historian and journalist Gwynne Dyer gives a long UBC talk on how climate change will reshape international politics. He covers food, borders, refugees and the possibility of unilateral geoengineering by affected nations.
Mc_4Z1oiXhY.why: HN recommends it as a sobering, still-relevant look at the geopolitical consequences of warming, including why official reports lag the data.

M6vpFV6Wkl4.summary: Gary Taubes presents the argument of his book Why We Get Fat to Googlers in 2011. He claims the type of calories matters more than the count, challenges calories-in-calories-out thinking and criticizes the low-fat dietary consensus.
M6vpFV6Wkl4.why: Recommended in diet and weight-loss threads as the accessible case for the carbohydrate-insulin view of obesity.

MBRqu0YOH14.summary: Kurzgesagt's short animated take on optimistic nihilism. It argues the universe has no inherent meaning, so we are free to create our own and enjoy life.
MBRqu0YOH14.why: HN users recommend it as a comforting, clear introduction to nihilism for anxiety, mid-life doubts and feeling behind in life.

MvgN5gCuLac.summary: George Carlin's classic stand-up routine about 'stuff' and how much of life is spent accumulating and storing it, from Comic Relief 1986. It satirizes American consumerism and possessions.
MvgN5gCuLac.why: HN keeps linking it in threads on clutter, storage units, real estate and consumerism as a perfectly apt comic take.

MBnnXbOM5S4.summary: 3Blue1Brown shows how the uncertainty principle arises from Fourier transforms. A wave packet cannot be narrow in both position and frequency, so the principle is a property of waves rather than of measurement.
MBnnXbOM5S4.why: HN recommends it as the clearest visual explanation that uncertainty is intrinsic to waves, separate from measurement disturbance.

ML4tw_UzqZE.summary: The first episode of Clickspring's series on reproducing the Antikythera Mechanism by hand, laying out the plan and the history. The series follows a machinist building the ancient Greek device with traditional tools and methods.
ML4tw_UzqZE.why: HN repeatedly recommends the series for its extraordinary craftsmanship and its credible demonstration of how the mechanism could have been made.

MZvmYaFkNJI.summary: Phoenix creator Chris McCord builds a real-time Twitter-style app live with Phoenix LiveView 1.5 in about 15 minutes. It shows interactive, real-time updates without writing JavaScript.
MZvmYaFkNJI.why: HN points people to it as the demo that shows why LiveView and Elixir are worth a look.

MijmeoH9LT4.summary: Tom Scott explains for Computerphile how Unicode and UTF-8 grew out of messy older character encodings to become the web's standard. It covers why the design works and how it handles worldwide text.
MijmeoH9LT4.why: HN treats it as the go-to short explanation of UTF-8, praised for making the topic stick.

MFRWDuduuSw.summary: The preface to Herb Gross's MIT OpenCourseWare 'Calculus Revisited: Single Variable Calculus', an older black-and-white lecture series. It introduces his approach to teaching calculus from the basics.
MFRWDuduuSw.why: HN recommends Herb Gross as an unusually clear teacher whose explanations make calculus click for people who struggled elsewhere.

M3BM9TB-8yA.summary: Node.js creator Ryan Dahl discusses ten design mistakes he made in Node, including package.json, npm, and module resolution. The talk sets out the motivations behind his later project, Deno.
M3BM9TB-8yA.why: HN treats it as the classic talk on why Deno exists and on lessons from design mistakes in a widely used platform.

MBT1OK6VAIU.summary: David Crane, designer of Pitfall for the Atari 2600, gives a GDC 2011 postmortem on the game's design challenges. He covers how he fit a large world into the console's tiny memory. The session ends with Q&A.
MBT1OK6VAIU.why: HN cites it for the story of how Pitfall's levels are generated procedurally from a seeded counter, within 4K of ROM.

MRqh8oLY7Ik.summary: David Heinemeier Hansson explains what he learned about indoor air quality after his new house made his family sick. He covers CO2, VOCs, off-gassing, HVAC and ventilation, and cognitive effects, presented at a Basecamp meetup.
MRqh8oLY7Ik.why: HN points to it as a fascinating talk that convinced many to buy air quality monitors, with citations to studies.

MdmQUlD7P40.summary: Matt Might's Curry On talk on ending errors in code, both software and the human genome. He covers conservative approximation of the halting problem via static analysis and a computational approach to precision medicine.
MdmQUlD7P40.why: Recommended as a jaw-dropping, must-see talk that gives an amazing intro to static analysis alongside Might's personal story.

MkJkyMuBm3g.summary: Rob Landley compares Toybox and BusyBox and surveys options for embedded system command-line tools, including GNU. He also tells the story of leaving BusyBox, Toybox becoming Android's command line, and licensing.
MkJkyMuBm3g.why: HN recommends it for the toybox intro and for Landley's candid account of software licensing and why he created the 0BSD license.

MsbiO8EAsGw.summary: Ben Krasnow of Applied Science explains how electrophoretic e-paper displays work and how he modified the driver firmware and waveform lookup tables of a 4.2-inch panel to reach roughly 3Hz partial refresh. It covers the tweakable constants in the refresh process and touches on colored e-ink microcapsules.
MsbiO8EAsGw.why: Whenever e-ink refresh speed or driving waveforms come up, HN points to this as the clearest hands-on explanation of how these displays work and how to hack them.

MtzCLd93SyU.summary: Civilization creator Sid Meier's GDC 2010 talk on applying psychology to game design. He discusses player perception, randomness, and win states, and why designers must account for how players experience events.
MtzCLd93SyU.why: HN people cite it when discussing perceived randomness, luck and player experience in games, and say more designers should heed it.

M4AhABManTw.summary: Jon Bois tells the story of the 1904 St. Louis Olympic marathon, a chaotic race involving fraud, rat poison, brandy, feral dogs and near-deaths. It is an episode of his show Pretty Good.
M4AhABManTw.why: HN commenters recommend it as a funny, well-told retelling of one of the strangest sporting events ever.

MFzDaBzBlL0.summary: Destin of Smarter Every Day learns to ride a bicycle whose steering is reversed, taking about eight months, and compares it with how his young son learned much faster. It illustrates knowledge versus understanding and brain plasticity in adults versus children.
MFzDaBzBlL0.why: HN cites it widely in discussions of tacit knowledge, habit, unlearning and adult versus child learning.

MQyxG4vTyZ8.summary: A Vox Borders episode with Johnny Harris explaining how China is gradually erasing the line between mainland China and Hong Kong since the 1997 handover. It describes the one country, two systems arrangement and its expiration date.
MQyxG4vTyZ8.why: HN commenters recommend it as a concise, captivating introduction to the Hong Kong conflict during the 2019 extradition-law protests.

MjdpR-TY6QU.summary: A Kurzgesagt animated explainer on whether aging could be cured within our lifetimes, made with Lifespan.io and the LEAF foundation. It introduces the idea of treating aging as a medical problem.
MjdpR-TY6QU.why: HN recommends it as an accessible introduction to longevity research that changed some commenters' views.

Mw9qiV7XlFs.summary: A two-hour driver's-eye cab ride along the Bernina railway from St. Moritz in Switzerland to Tirano in Italy. The UNESCO-listed line crosses the Alps at high altitude with steep adhesion gradients.
Mw9qiV7XlFs.why: Recommended as relaxing slow-TV, a long scenic video to unwind with.

Mz3JeYfBTcY.summary: Emily Shea, a Fastly engineer with repetitive strain injury, describes using voice dictation as her main way of programming. She covers homophones, custom vocabulary and building her own voice commands to write Perl.
Mz3JeYfBTcY.why: HN treats it as a phenomenal demonstration that voice-driven development is viable and as an eye-opener on accessibility-unfriendly coding habits.

M8F5hXqS-Ac.summary: Not Just Bikes compares the same cycling trip to a hardware store in Calgary and in Amsterdam, using a 'plus 1 minus 2' format. It shows how street design shapes how safe and practical cycling is.
M8F5hXqS-Ac.why: HN recommends the channel for understanding why North American road design makes cycling dangerous and how the Dutch approach differs.

MFol6IMbZ7Y.summary: Moxie Marlinspike's Black Hat talk presenting sslstrip, which defeats SSL in practice by intercepting the http-to-https redirect.
MFol6IMbZ7Y.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining talk and the original source on the stripping attack that motivated HSTS.

MO0r930Sn_8.summary: A short clip of Richard Feynman answering an interviewer's question about how magnets work, in which he explains why a why-question has no simple answer without a shared frame of reference.
MO0r930Sn_8.why: HN returns to it constantly as a classic on the difficulty of explaining fundamentals and the limits of analogies.

MYucYon2-lk.summary: Hillel Wayne's PyCon 2018 talk on testing beyond pytest and mypy. It introduces property-based testing with the Hypothesis library and design-by-contract with dpcontracts, and shows how to combine them with an existing test suite.
MYucYon2-lk.why: HN commenters point to it as a concise, convincing case for better testing practice short of full formal methods.

MiUHjLxm3V0.summary: Veritasium explains how ASML's EUV lithography machines make the most advanced computer chips, covering the engineering of the light source, mirrors and the supply chain around them. It is a long-form explainer on the world's most complex commercial machine.
MiUHjLxm3V0.why: HN commenters recommend it as the accessible deep-dive on EUV lithography and why chip manufacturing is so hard.

MondapIjAAM.summary: Climate Town tells the history of the period when the greenhouse effect was not politically controversial and the US came close to acting on climate. It covers Exxon's early climate science and the policy failures that followed.
MondapIjAAM.why: HN recommends it as an entertaining summary of early bipartisan climate action and corporate influence on research.

MCVj5RZOqwY.summary: Avi Bryant demos Dabble DB, a web-based spreadsheet-like database for building apps without code. It shows how users can model and relate data through a smooth interface.
MCVj5RZOqwY.why: HN points to it as a lost example of intuitive low-code tooling, and as inspiration for newer products.

MEUWxNifJJ8.summary: Yanis Varoufakis talks at a festival in Zagreb about his book The Global Minotaur. He argues the postwar global economy and the 2008 crisis stem from deeper structural causes than greed or weak regulation.
MEUWxNifJJ8.why: HN recommends it as a narrative of a century of political economy and the geopolitics behind the 2008 crash.

MHTizZ_XcUM.summary: Mark Rober shows an automatic bullseye dartboard that tracks a thrown dart with motion capture and moves in real time so it always hits the center. He spent over three years on the project.
MHTizZ_XcUM.why: HN calls it a great, impressive engineering project involving real-time trajectory calculation.

MShbP3OpASA.summary: Linus Torvalds is interviewed at Aalto University in 2012, followed by an audience Q&A. He talks about Linux, kernel development and the desktop, and about Nvidia support. The Q&A has a well-known moment where he is blunt about Nvidia.
MShbP3OpASA.why: HN links it for individual clips: the Nvidia moment, his views on C and his blunt communication style. Some commenters say the whole talk is worth watching.

M_VuXVErD6E.summary: Ben Vallack walks through designing a custom keyboard PCB from scratch using Ergogen and KiCad, ending with a gerber file ready to order from a PCB fabricator. The example is a split keyboard.
M_VuXVErD6E.why: HN recommends it as a thorough, general walkthrough of the steps in designing your own keyboard.

MgrO5za0lSY.summary: A BBC documentary on Francis Bacon, the loud, hard-drinking British painter, drawing on people who knew him. It explores the haunted man behind the Roaring Boy persona.
MgrO5za0lSY.why: HN commenters recommend it as a well-made, interesting and sad documentary on Bacon's troubled life.

MlhAkNWC1qo.summary: David Heinemeier Hansson, creator of Ruby on Rails and partner at 37signals, argues that planning is guessing and startups should focus on today. He says constraints are an advantage and that startups can bootstrap profitably in sizable markets.
MlhAkNWC1qo.why: HN recommends it as the classic counterpoint to Silicon Valley growth-at-all-costs startup thinking.

Mlrrc_vy79E.summary: David Brevik's GDC 2016 post-mortem of the original Diablo, covering how it evolved from a turn-based claymation DOS game into the genre-defining action RPG. It includes development anecdotes and lessons learned.
Mlrrc_vy79E.why: HN considers it one of the best GDC post-mortems, with funny anecdotes (such as turning down Hotmail equity) and multiplayer insights.

Mvse4Xhzwuk.summary: AVweb's Paul Bertorelli explains in part two of a series why general aviation has not replaced leaded avgas. He covers industry inertia, bureaucratic delays and the exemption that lets the industry keep using lead.
Mvse4Xhzwuk.why: HN recommends the series for explaining why unleaded avgas has been so hard to approve, usually in threads about FAA and EPA fuel decisions.

M1ONXea0mXg.summary: SoundHound's CEO demos Hound, a voice assistant, handling fast compound natural language queries with context and detailed criteria. The video leaked before the product's official launch.
M1ONXea0mXg.why: HN viewers were impressed by its speed and saw it as a glimpse of the future of voice search; later it appears in hiring posts.

MVYrJJNdrEg.summary: Lex Fridman interviews Mark Zuckerberg in the metaverse, with both appearing as photorealistic avatars from separate locations. They discuss Meta's AI, VR and the future of avatars.
MVYrJJNdrEg.why: HN points to it as a demonstration that VR presence can feel close to talking in person.

McLq1hEq3UY.summary: The introductory lecture of Stephen Boyd's Stanford Convex Optimization I course (EE 364A). It outlines convex sets, functions and problems, and the course's coverage of least-squares, linear and semidefinite programming, duality and interior-point methods.
McLq1hEq3UY.why: HN recommends Boyd's lectures as a fantastic, often funny follow-up to linear algebra and as a step in machine learning study paths.

MnrJzXM7a6o.summary: An excerpt from Steve Jobs's January 2007 Macworld keynote in which he introduces the original iPhone. It shows the pitch of a phone, music player and internet communicator, along with the live demo.
MnrJzXM7a6o.why: HN treats it as the model product demo and MVP showcase, and as a reminder of how constrained the first iPhone hardware was.

MzzD2F73iGU.summary: An episode of Adam Savage's Still Untitled podcast with molecular biologist Joe DeRisi. They discuss his work, including sequencing to detect rare infections, in a conversation Savage calls possibly the show's scariest.
MzzD2F73iGU.why: HN recommends it for DeRisi's fascinating stories about rare pathogens such as brain-eating amoebas.

M2fKMP47slQ.summary: Malte Skarupke's C++Now 2018 talk on hash table performance, explaining why std::unordered_map is slow and memory hungry and presenting faster designs, including his bytell hash map.
M2fKMP47slQ.why: Recommended as a thorough, well-regarded explanation of hash table design tradeoffs and why the standard container is a poor choice.

MEqxaH47DTs.summary: Engineering Explained compares the lifetime CO2 emissions of a Toyota RAV4 Prime plug-in hybrid with a Tesla Model Y, looking at break-even mileage and whether electric cars are worse for the environment.
MEqxaH47DTs.why: HN cites it for reasonable estimates comparing the emissions of EVs, hybrids and ICE cars.

MGMoRu5yrVc.summary: A CppCon 2014 talk by Microsoft engineers on how Office delivers a single-source C++ codebase across iOS, Android, Windows and Mac. It covers architectures, techniques and lessons from shipping cross-platform products.
MGMoRu5yrVc.why: Cited in Electron, Flutter and React Native debates as evidence that large products can share C++ core code with native views.

MGfhQTbcqmA.summary: UCLA professor Dario Nardi presents brain-imaging research suggesting that different Myers-Briggs personality types use their brains in different ways. He discusses how each type can reach a state of creative flow. It is aimed at a general audience.
MGfhQTbcqmA.why: HN cites it in MBTI threads as an attempt to link personality types to measurable brain activity patterns.

MNXypBxNGMo.summary: Gameplay footage of Zarch, the 1987 3D Defender-like game by David Braben for the Acorn Archimedes. It shows the 256-colour 3D landscape where you stop landers spreading a virus.
MNXypBxNGMo.why: HN commenters recall it as a mind-blowing early 3D game that showed what the Archimedes hardware could do.

MO8hZlgK5zc.summary: C J Silverio, former npm CTO, explains how the JavaScript package commons ended up in the hands of a for-profit company with no accountability. She discusses the cost of running a registry and what the community should do next.
MO8hZlgK5zc.why: HN recommends it as the best account of what is wrong with npm's governance and why alternative or decentralized registries are hard.

MSZgoFyuHC8.summary: A satirical 'Honest Government Ad' from The Juice Media that mocks Australian carbon capture and storage policy. It lays out the fossil fuel industry's influence and the weak results of the technology in a comedic format.
MSZgoFyuHC8.why: HN links it as a funny but fact-based critique of carbon capture in climate and energy threads.

MVEKt_H3FsI.summary: Part two of a Computer History Museum oral history with Gary Davidian, covering his work on the 68000 emulator for PowerPC at Apple, Power Computing, clean-room contracting and later performance optimization work. It is nearly three hours long.
MVEKt_H3FsI.why: Pointed to as a primary-source interview on Apple's architecture transitions, emulation and microcode work.

MWsGBRdK2N0.summary: Not Just Bikes explains that car-dependent suburbs are not the only option, using Toronto's Riverdale as an example of a pre-war streetcar suburb. These walkable neighborhoods are popular but are now effectively illegal to build.
MWsGBRdK2N0.why: HN cites it in zoning, density and housing threads as an illustration of the missing middle between city center and car-dependent sprawl.

MejbOFk7H6c.summary: OK Go's music video for Needing/Getting, shot in the desert with a Chevy Sonic fitted with pneumatic arms that play over a thousand instruments across two miles.
MejbOFk7H6c.why: Recommended as an example of inventive, physical-effects music video making, with the car as an instrument.

Mjx3S3UjmnA.summary: An MTA video on communications-based train control, the system meant to replace the New York City subway's century-old signaling. It also shows the mechanical interlocks and signals in use today.
Mjx3S3UjmnA.why: Cited as a view into how outdated and error-prone NYC subway signaling is, and how antique interlocking systems work.

MmG2ah5Df4g.summary: ScienceClic gives a 15-minute animated introduction to quantum field theory, covering fields, spin, conserved quantities, the standard model and interactions.
MmG2ah5Df4g.why: Offered as an accessible visualization for people wanting to understand particles as excitations of fields.

MnyeRlMsTgI.summary: Not Just Bikes argues that North American transit struggles to attract riders because of the land use around it, not the transit itself. It uses examples such as a London, Ontario line with unreachable stations.
MnyeRlMsTgI.why: Recommended in transit threads as a clear video essay on why American transit fails: infrequent, isolated and car-oriented surroundings.

MpfvhiqFw7A.summary: An 8-minute explainer on the Lightning Network and how it relates to Segwit, Bitcoin and Litecoin. It covers how off-chain payment channels route payments to scale blockchain transactions.
MpfvhiqFw7A.why: Commenters point to it as a short, high-level overview of how Lightning payment channels work.

MtxA20Q-Uss.summary: The final part of Dan Gelbart's 18-part Building Prototypes series, focused on mechanical design. It opens with a demonstration of stiffness and covers practical design principles for prototype machines.
MtxA20Q-Uss.why: HN recommends it, and the whole series, for practical mechanical design insight such as how structures achieve stiffness.

Mx-AllVZ1VY.summary: Keynote from the 2016 Dart Developer Summit introducing Flutter, Google's toolkit for building mobile apps from one codebase. It shows early demos aimed at native look and feel.
Mx-AllVZ1VY.why: Recommended as the early introduction to Flutter's single-codebase iOS and Android approach.

My4RA5I0FKs.summary: Mark Rober builds a hot tub filled with sand fluidized by air blown from below, so that the sand behaves like a liquid. He explains how fluidized beds work and shows people swimming in them.
My4RA5I0FKs.why: HN mentions it as the famous, kid-delighting demo of fluidization, especially in sand battery and industrial process threads.

MOvfn1p92_8.summary: A GameTrailers walkthrough from E3 2012 of an Unreal Engine 4 real-time tech demo with Epic's Alan Willard. It shows live code changes and hot reloading while the game runs.
MOvfn1p92_8.why: HN cites it as a favorite demo of live coding and hot reload in a game engine.

MzRCDLre1b4.summary: 3Blue1Brown, in collaboration with minutephysics, introduces the math of superposition and quantum states using polarized light. It builds up the quantum behavior of photons as a simple counting and probability problem.
MzRCDLre1b4.why: Recommended as an approachable way to understand the quantum nature of light and basic quantum math without heavy machinery.

MBVmnKuBocc.summary: Associate Professor Simon Michaux presents estimates of the metals needed to build one generation of renewable technology to replace fossil fuels. He argues current production and reserves fall far short, with copper a key shortfall.
MBVmnKuBocc.why: Cited in energy transition threads for ballpark numbers on mineral demand, though some commenters criticize its assumptions.

MQufJBVvAtY.summary: Loopop reviews the Polyend Tracker hardware tracker-style sequencer and walks through a tutorial from sampling to finishing a song. It covers most of the device's features.
MQufJBVvAtY.why: HN mentions it as a good high-level tutorial when threads on tracker music and the Amiga scene come up.

MRpEV2tmYz4.summary: A short clip of Milton Friedman clearing up misconceptions about redistribution of wealth and inheritance tax, arguing that a heavy inheritance tax encourages wasteful behavior.
MRpEV2tmYz4.why: HN cites it in debates on wealth taxes, inheritance and inequality as Friedman's argument against redistribution.

MUdro-6u2Zg.summary: Ben Krasnow of Applied Science shows that a plain laser diode can measure sub-micron vibrations from centimeters away using self-mixing interferometry, and can also be used for range-finding.
MUdro-6u2Zg.why: HN points to it as a cool demonstration of cheap precision laser measurement and the origin of hacks based on self-mixing.

MYGJ9jrbpvg.summary: Theo Jansen shows many of his Strandbeests, wind-powered walking kinetic sculptures, set to Khachaturian's Spartacus. It presents his work since 1990 on creating new forms of life on beaches.
MYGJ9jrbpvg.why: HN links it in Strandbeest threads as a showcase of the eerily smooth, wind-driven walking creatures.

Ma9FrN5COIo.summary: A hobbyist builds a prototype full-frame CCD camera from scratch, with open-source design files and a custom PCB. The video shows the first, still rough prototype.
Ma9FrN5COIo.why: HN points to it as an example of advanced DIY hardware, specifically a camera using an affordable Kodak CCD sensor with global shutter.

MeMPCSqQ-34.summary: Ryan Gordon (Icculus) gives a high-level overview of SDL 2.0 at Steam Dev Days 2014. He covers its features and how it eases building, porting and maintaining games, including Linux ports.
MeMPCSqQ-34.why: HN commenters link it when people ask about cross-platform game development and for details like SDL's licensing change.

MesrrYyuoa4.summary: A clip from the 2015 film The Big Short in which FrontPoint Partners investigate mortgage lending in Florida and place their first trade. It shows brokers and a stripper-adjacent loan scene illustrating subprime lending to unverified borrowers.
MesrrYyuoa4.why: Cited as a film scene illustrating subprime lending, housing bubbles, and people bragging about bad behavior.

Mh5LY4Mz15o.summary: Bill Wurtz's fast, comedic and musical run through the whole history of Japan in nine minutes.
Mh5LY4Mz15o.why: HN mentions it as an entertaining quick history, and as a stylistic reference or joke in threads about history and the creator's other videos.

MhQ70O1MiXc.summary: Footage of Notch (Markus Persson) live-coding his Minicraft game in Java during a Ludum Dare 48-hour game jam. It shows a working game developer building a complete small game from scratch.
MhQ70O1MiXc.why: HN points to it as an example of Notch's famous live-coding sessions, which drew many early Minecraft fans.

MkeS_0NQUZs.summary: Institute for Justice footage of Nevada Highway Patrol troopers seizing the life savings of Stephen Lara, a retired Marine, during a traffic stop under civil forfeiture. The video documents the stop and the case that followed.
MkeS_0NQUZs.why: HN commenters cite it as a concrete example of police seizing cash from innocent people on flimsy pretexts.

Mq785nJ0FXQ.summary: John Oliver's Last Week Tonight segment on daily fantasy sports, arguing the sites are effectively gambling operations despite their claims. It mocks their advertising and the skill-versus-chance defence.
Mq785nJ0FXQ.why: HN uses it as the canonical link whenever daily fantasy sports comes up.

Mri66Uz6-8Y.summary: Jordan Hubbard, FreeBSD co-founder, discusses where FreeBSD might go over the next decade at MeetBSD California 2014. He draws on his Apple Unix experience, including bringing launchd-style init ideas to FreeBSD.
Mri66Uz6-8Y.why: Cited in init-system and Unix debates as FreeBSD's stance on launchd versus systemd, and recommended for its view of FreeBSD's future.

MtSE4rglxbY.summary: Alain de Botton gives a TED talk questioning how we define success and failure. He argues that snobbery and the assumption that outcomes are fully earned make career anxiety worse.
MtSE4rglxbY.why: HN cites it in discussions of wealth, status and the moral blame placed on the unsuccessful.

MvRTALJp8DM.summary: A demonstration from UPenn's GRASP Lab of an autonomous quadrotor performing flips, flying through windows and perching on surfaces. It shows precise aggressive maneuvering control of a small UAV.
MvRTALJp8DM.why: Cited as a landmark demonstration of how capable autonomous drones had become, mostly in threads about drone delivery, swarms and drone warfare.

MxT6IwUtLSU.summary: A Gaming Historian documentary on the creation of Super Mario Bros. 3, the hype around its release and why it is regarded as one of the greatest games. It runs about 50 minutes in three parts.
MxT6IwUtLSU.why: HN mentions it for the game design history it contains and as part of a list of good gaming history channels.

Myq_Hc_39aI.summary: A roughly two and a half hour Noonautics panel on DMT research moderated by Graham Hancock with Andrew Gallimore and Rick Strassman. It discusses planned DMTx experiments and reported DMT experiences.
Myq_Hc_39aI.why: HN points to it when discussing DMT research and reports of contact with entity-like beings.

M16CGK1T9MM.summary: Half as Interesting explains why the Eiffel Tower's night-time lighting is under copyright, which makes publishing photos of it at night legally problematic.
M16CGK1T9MM.why: It is the go-to reference in copyright threads for the oddity that the tower's night view is protected.

M9cSxEqKQ78.summary: Team BlackSheep flies FPV (first-person view) model aircraft over New York City, past the Brooklyn and Verrazano bridges, lower Manhattan and the Statue of Liberty. The flights stirred controversy in the RC community.
M9cSxEqKQ78.why: HN cites it as a well-known early example of FPV drone flight in drone and regulation discussions.

M9xMuPWAZW8.summary: A spectrogram analysis of Aphex Twin's track commonly called [Equation] from Windowlicker, rendered from a lossless version. At about 5:30 the spectrogram reveals an image of Richard D. James's face.
M9xMuPWAZW8.why: HN uses it as the canonical example of hiding images in audio spectrograms.

MCBdcNA_FsI.summary: A WSJ report on China's 'dark factories', highly automated plants run by robots with little human presence, visiting Zeekr's EV factory. It covers Chinese labor costs, automation and overproduction in the EV industry.
MCBdcNA_FsI.why: HN cites it as evidence that lights-out factories exist, though one commenter notes it is outdated relative to current automation.

MIHC4NNScEI.summary: A 30-minute edit of a conversation between Adam Curtis and Russell Brand in which Curtis explains HyperNormalisation and his ideas on individualism, power and real change.
MIHC4NNScEI.why: HN refers to it as a compact source for the term HyperNormalisation and the idea of a constructed fake world.

MK0SrxBC1xs.summary: WIRED's Andy Greenberg drives a Jeep on a highway while two hackers take control of it remotely over the internet. They manipulate the car and then cut the engine. The video accompanies the 2015 article on the Jeep Cherokee hack.
MK0SrxBC1xs.why: HN cites it as the standard precedent for remote car hacking whenever connected or self-driving vehicle security comes up.

MMaGnpVaSGQ.summary: A scene from Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home in which Kirk and crew rescue the injured Chekov from a 20th-century hospital.
MMaGnpVaSGQ.why: HN commenters post it as a joke about primitive medicine whenever a thread covers medical failures or old-fashioned treatment.

MOXQo7nURs0.summary: An IKEA Singapore ad parodying Apple product launches by presenting the 2015 catalogue as a revolutionary 'bookbook' device. It is a short, tongue-in-cheek spoof of Apple-style marketing.
MOXQo7nURs0.why: HN brings it up as a favorite Apple parody, mostly as a joke when books or Apple design come up.

MPHUu9sAGKo.summary: Sam Harris interviews linguist John McWhorter about race, racism and what McWhorter calls the new religion of anti-racism. Topics include identity politics, police violence and affirmative action.
